regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Maintenance after a response to platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Oral PARP-inhibitor maintenance after a complete or partial response to platinum. Distinguish first-line advanced high-grade disease from platinum-sensitive relapsed high-grade serous disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Maintenance after a response to platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Niraparib: Niraparib blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA. This can slow the growth of some cancer cells.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take the prescribed dose once every day. A 28-day cycle is a way of recording treatment. There is no planned tablet-free week.
key_points: The NCCP lists blood pressure at week 2, monthly for 6 months and then every 3 months. The European product information calls for at least weekly readings for the first 2 months, monthly during the first year and periodically thereafter. Agree a written monitoring plan with your team before starting.

PRIMA studied first-line maintenance after platinum response. The risk of progression or death was lower with niraparib than placebo in the homologous-recombination-deficient group (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59). NOVA separately studied maintenance after platinum-sensitive relapse.
The first-line and relapse studies enrolled different populations. Delayed progression is a group result and does not establish a survival benefit for an individual.
Follow your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Bedtime dosing may help nausea. Speak to the team before changing the dose or stopping.
Show your team all medicines, including blood thinners, aspirin and supplements. Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own.
Niraparib can harm a developing baby. Discuss contraception, fertility and breastfeeding before starting.
Check the clinical setting, pretreatment weight and baseline platelets when selecting a starting dose. A treatment interruption requires the nadir, affected lineage, elapsed time and previous dose.
NCCP Table 3 and the SmPC differ for hepatic impairment. Confirm the intended dose and feasible tablet strength with oncology pharmacy.

NCCP 00862 Table 1, adverse-event dose reductions: from 300 mg once daily, the reduced levels are 200 mg then 100 mg; from 200 mg once daily, the reduced level is 100 mg. If a further reduction below 100 mg is required, discontinue. Confirm the prescribed dose, previous reductions and event-specific recovery criteria before restarting.

administration.route_and_duration: Swallow the tablets whole with water at the same time each day, either with a light meal or at least one hour before or two hours after food. If you miss a dose or vomit after it, take the next scheduled dose. Do not take an extra tablet.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: First-line treatment for dMMR/MSI-H primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. Six combination cycles are followed by single-agent dostarlimab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Dostarlimab: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs. Paclitaxel: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected. Carboplatin: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Three medicines every 3 weeks for six planned cycles. The first Jemperli-only visit is 3 weeks after cycle six. After that, Jemperli is given every 6 weeks.
key_points: Immune inflammation can start between visits or after treatment ends. Keep the immunotherapy alert card and show it to every team caring for you.
In RUBY, adding dostarlimab to chemotherapy and then continuing dostarlimab reduced the hazard of progression or death in the dMMR/MSI-H group (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.16–0.50).
These results compare groups over time. They cannot predict the duration of benefit for one person. The NCCP indication shown here is biomarker-specific.
Carboplatin carries high sickness risk. Follow the scheduled anti-sickness medicines and the rescue plan given by your team.
Before paclitaxel the unit provides medicines to reduce allergic reactions. Confirm any doses you must take at home before attending.
Sickness risk is minimal with Jemperli alone. Ask which medicines continue once chemotherapy ends. Keep carrying your immunotherapy alert card.
Initial administration order: dostarlimab over 30 minutes, paclitaxel over 3 hours, then carboplatin over 30 minutes. Confirm infusion sets and filters against the official protocol.

Do not reduce dostarlimab for chemotherapy count thresholds. Attribute immune toxicity, grade and recurrence before a permanent discontinuation decision. Use the liver-metastasis exception where applicable.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: The aim is to control womb cancer that is advanced or has returned, and delay it getting worse.
patient_selection.disease_and_biomarker_context: First-line treatment for dMMR/MSI-H primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. Six combination cycles are followed by single-agent dostarlimab maintenance.
eligibility_orientation: dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
important_cautions: Do not reduce dostarlimab for chemotherapy count thresholds. Attribute immune toxicity, grade and recurrence before a permanent discontinuation decision. Use the liver-metastasis exception where applicable.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Three medicines every 3 weeks for six planned cycles. The first Jemperli-only visit is 3 weeks after cycle six. After that, Jemperli is given every 6 weeks.
administration.route_and_duration: On combination days, dostarlimab goes into a vein first, then paclitaxel, then carboplatin. The paclitaxel infusion usually takes about three hours. Allow extra time for checks, premedicines and observation.
practical_workflow: Three infusions every three weeks if your team confirms you are ready.
Jemperli alone, then every six weeks. Your team reviews benefit and side effects. NCCP allows up to three years of monotherapy.
observation_and_access: Monitor during each infusion. Use separate agent-specific infusion instructions and emergency procedures.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High with carboplatin during combination; minimal for dostarlimab maintenance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Confirm taxane premedication before combination therapy and reconcile corticosteroid exposure.
patient_education: Carboplatin carries high sickness risk. Follow the scheduled anti-sickness medicines and the rescue plan given by your team.
Before paclitaxel the unit provides medicines to reduce allergic reactions. Confirm any doses you must take at home before attending.
Sickness risk is minimal with Jemperli alone. Ask which medicines continue once chemotherapy ends. Keep carrying your immunotherapy alert card.
special_support: Use the regimen-specific supportive-care PDF and local prescription.

baseline: Tumour result, blood counts, liver, kidneys, glucose and thyroid
before_each_cycle: Bloods and glucose before each cycle. Check skin and neuropathy.
ongoing: Immune inflammation can start between visits or after treatment ends. Keep the immunotherapy alert card and show it to every team caring for you.
priority_toxicities: Dostarlimab: Immune inflammation, Hormone changes, Infusion reaction
Paclitaxel: Nerve symptoms, Hair loss, Allergic reaction
Carboplatin: Low blood counts, Nausea, Infusion reaction
urgent_review_signals: Lung, bowel, liver, kidney, skin and hormone problems can begin after treatment stops. Call urgently for new breathlessness, diarrhoea, jaundice or marked weakness.
Fever, chills, bleeding or sudden illness need an immediate call. Report flushing, dizziness or wheeze during any infusion immediately.

cells: Confirm dMMR/MSI-H, eligibility and baseline tests.

evidence_records.publication_title: PRIMA · First-line maintenance after response to platinum for advanced ovarian cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line maintenance after response to platinum for advanced ovarian cancer
key_findings: HRD subgroup: hazard ratio for progression or death 0.43 (95% CI 0.31–0.59).
evidence_records.limitations: The final overall survival analysis did not show an overall survival difference. Interpret the initial progression-free survival endpoint separately.

evidence_records.publication_title: NOVA · Maintenance after response in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Maintenance after response in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer
key_findings: Median progression-free survival in the germline BRCA-mutated cohort was 21.0 versus 5.5 months.
evidence_records.limitations: The biomarker cohorts and relapse setting matter when counselling. These medians do not predict an individual outcome.

evidence_records.publication_title: RUBY · Primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
key_findings: dMMR/MSI-H subgroup: hazard ratio for progression or death 0.28 (95% CI 0.16–0.50).
evidence_records.limitations: The overall study population is broader than the biomarker-defined population of the Irish protocol. Report the applicable subgroup.
